meta.title: zapi-cli — Zoho API CLI for AI Agents
meta.sourceOfTruth: tech_spec/ directory. The tech_spec files are the only source of truth.

documentInventory.covers: Full PRD: product overview, goals, personas, functional requirements, UX, narrative, success metrics, technical considerations, milestones, user stories (ZAPI-001–ZAPI-024)

Technical specification: solution structure, project layout, command tree, global flags, output contract, data models, auth flows, ZohoCorp restriction, storage paths, API client, trace sessions, dependency list, non-goals

Project vision and design exploration: agent-first design rationale, platform choices, PAT/OAuth flows, account metadata, scope lifecycle, storage layout, API base-URL strategy, host allowlist, trace design, Pex/WebSocket future ideas
Decision: .NET 10 / C# 13 as runtime and language; self-contained single-file binary per platform RID
Decision: pluggable IAuthProvider with PatAuthProvider in v1; OAuthProvider as a v2 drop-in; compile-time OAuth client credentials
Decision: --base-url required on every api call; no product-to-subdomain derivation; API Registry shorthand deferred to v2
Decision: OS-native keychain via P/Invoke (no NuGet package) with AES-256-GCM encrypted-file fallback for headless environments
Decision: hard-block any account whose email's second-level domain label equals 'zohocorp'; compile-time constant; no runtime override
Decision: compile-time sealed allowlist of Zoho host suffixes; HOST_NOT_ALLOWED pre-request if host not matched; SSRF prevention
Decision: always-on session-scoped tracing (no per-call flag); silent drop when no session active; named sessions; non-destructive export; Authorization header always excluded

projectSummary.name: zapi-cli
projectSummary.description: A standalone, self-contained command-line binary providing a deterministic, scriptable interface to any Zoho product's REST APIs. Manages multiple Zoho accounts, handles authentication via a pluggable IAuthProvider interface (PAT in v1, OAuth2 in v2), and exposes a general-purpose HTTP API invoker where the caller supplies the full base URL at invocation time.
primaryConsumers: AI agents — GitHub Copilot CLI Skills and Claude Agent Skills that invoke zapi-cli as a subprocess
Human developers — light use for account setup, ad-hoc API calls, and trace session inspection
projectSummary.coreWorkflow: Agent or human invokes `zapi-cli <command-group> <command> [flags]` → zapi-cli resolves account, validates host allowlist (pre-request), injects Authorization header, dispatches HTTP request to Zoho product API → structured JSON to stdout (success) or stderr (error).
keyProperties: Single self-contained binary, .NET 10 / C# 13, no runtime pre-install required on target machine
Platforms: macOS (Intel + Apple Silicon), Windows x64, Linux x64
Auth: PAT-first via IAuthProvider; OS-native keychain (P/Invoke, no NuGet) or AES-256-GCM encrypted file fallback
--base-url required on every api call; final URL assembled as <base-url><path>; no product-to-subdomain derivation
All stdout/stderr output is valid JSON; fixed symbolic error codes; exit codes 0 / 1 / 2
Compile-time HTTP host allowlist (SSRF prevention); ZohoCorp domain hard-block (unconditional, dual-layer)
Always-on session-scoped trace: api call auto-appends to active session JSONL without per-call flags; Authorization header always excluded from trace entries

business: Provide a single, self-contained binary that AI agents can invoke to perform authenticated Zoho API calls across any Zoho product.
Eliminate the need for product-specific Zoho CLI tools — one binary covers Cliq, Desk, CRM, People, Creator, and any other Zoho product via the caller-supplied --base-url pattern.
Deliver a fully runnable v1 CLI with all core use cases working end-to-end in a single development day.
user: AI agents: execute Zoho REST API calls non-interactively, parse structured JSON responses, manage account context across multi-step workflows, and export complete trace logs for debugging.
Human developers: configure Zoho accounts and their PAT tokens once, then leave the CLI to agents; inspect trace sessions when reviewing agent runs.
nonGoals: OAuth 2.0 authentication flow — deferred to v2.
WebSocket connections (ws group) — deferred to v2.
Pex / Zoho Cliq real-time protocol (pex group) — deferred to v2.
API Registry shorthand (api registry group) — deferred to v2.
Binary distribution, packaging, or publishing — address in a separate work item.
Support for ZohoCorp corporate accounts (*@zohocorp.com and datacenter variants) — hard-blocked unconditionally.
Any Zoho product-specific logic beyond authentication header injection.

personas.name: AI Agent (Copilot / Claude)
personas.description: A GitHub Copilot CLI Skill or Claude Agent Skill that invokes zapi-cli as a subprocess for each API interaction. Issues commands with structured flags, parses stdout JSON, branches on the 'code' field in stderr on failure. Always runs with --no-input.
needs: Machine-parseable JSON on stdout and stderr for every invocation
Fixed symbolic error code vocabulary — error-handling logic written once, works for all commands
No interactive prompts in any code path
Deterministic behavior: identical inputs always produce identical behavior

personas.name: Developer
personas.description: A software engineer who configures Zoho accounts on their machine and occasionally runs api call or trace session export directly in a terminal. Performs initial account setup; then the CLI is left entirely to agents.
needs: Simple one-shot account add command to configure PAT once
Readable (but still structured) output for account show and trace session export
Confidence that credentials are never written to disk in plaintext

roleBasedAccess.capabilities: Add, remove, show, list, and set-default accounts. Responsible for the PAT credential stored in the OS keychain. Access to Zoho APIs governed by the PAT's own permissions.

Inherits account permissions at the token level. Can call APIs, manage trace sessions, and run scope/utility commands. Cannot add or remove accounts — account configuration must be completed by a human before the agent is invoked.
Hard-blocked at account add, api call, and all scope commands regardless of invoker. Error code: ACCOUNT_DOMAIN_BLOCKED, exit 1. No override path exists.

functionalRequirements.description: Add, list, remove, show, set-default account operations with PAT authentication.
details: account add --name <n> --auth-type pat --token <t> [--domain <d>]: fetches email from Zoho user-info API for ZohoCorp domain check; stores PAT in OS keychain; writes metadata (without token) to accounts.json. --domain defaults to zoho.com.
account list: returns all accounts as JSON array with token values masked as '***'.
account remove --name <n>: deletes keychain secret and accounts.json entry; ACCOUNT_NOT_FOUND if missing.
account show --name <n>: returns full AccountEntry JSON with token masked as '***'.
account set-default --name <n>: sets is_default=true on named account; false on all others.
account re-auth --name <n>: stub in v1; fully activated with OAuth2 in v2.
All account operations support global --account override for per-command account selection.

functionalRequirements.description: OS-native keychain via P/Invoke with AES-256-GCM encrypted-file fallback for headless environments.
details: macOS: MacOsKeychainProvider — Security.framework (SecKeychainAddGenericPassword / SecKeychainFindGenericPassword).
Windows: WindowsKeychainProvider — advapi32.dll CredWrite / CredRead.
Linux: LinuxKeychainProvider — libsecret Secret Service API.
Fallback: EncryptedFileKeychainProvider — AES-256-GCM, key derived from machine entropy; activates automatically when OS keychain is unavailable.
No third-party NuGet keychain package — all implementations via direct P/Invoke.
Key naming convention: zapi-cli:<accountName>:<tokenType> (e.g., zapi-cli:work:pat).
Token values must never appear in accounts.json, stdout, stderr, or any trace file in plain text.

functionalRequirements.description: Make authenticated HTTP requests to any Zoho product API with configurable method, path, headers, query params, and body.
details:
api call --base-url --method --path

[--body |--body-file ] [--header k:v]... [--query k=v]... [--account ].
--base-url is required on every invocation; final URL assembled as <base-url><path>.
--body and --body-file are mutually exclusive; INVALID_ARGS if both supplied before any network I/O.
Host allowlist validated pre-request; HOST_NOT_ALLOWED (exit 1) if host not in allowlist.
ZohoCorp domain check applied to resolved account before any network activity.
Authorization: Zoho-oauthtoken <token> injected from resolved account's keychain secret.
Supported methods: GET, POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE.
Returns HTTP response as structured JSON to stdout on success.
Exits 1 on HTTP 4xx/5xx with error response in stderr JSON envelope.

functionalRequirements.description: Record OAuth scope metadata per account; sets needs_reauth lifecycle flag.
details: scope add --scope <s> [--account <n>]: appends scope string to account's scopes[]; sets needs_reauth=true; duplicate scopes not added.
scope remove --scope <s> [--account <n>]: removes scope; sets needs_reauth=true; SCOPE_NOT_FOUND if not present.
scope list [--account <n>]: returns scopes array as JSON; exits 0 even if empty.
api call targeting an account with needs_reauth=true returns NEEDS_REAUTH, exit 2, before any HTTP activity.
In v1, account re-auth is a stub; no token exchange attempted.

functionalRequirements.description: Always-on session-scoped trace: api call auto-appends to the active session JSONL without per-call flags.
details: trace session start --name <n>: creates active session; entry written to sessions.json; traces/<name>/trace.jsonl created empty.
While a session is active, every api call automatically appends an ApiTraceEntry to the session JSONL — no per-call flag required.
When no session is active, trace entries are silently dropped — no implicit session is created.
Starting a session when one is already active replaces the active session pointer; old session is preserved.
Authorization headers unconditionally excluded from all trace entries.
trace session list: returns JSON array of all sessions with name, start_time, entry_count, status.
trace session export --name <n> [--truncate-body <bytes>] [--type api|pex]: emits JSON array to stdout; non-destructive.
trace session close --name <n>: marks session as closed in sessions.json; JSONL preserved for export.
trace session remove --name <n>: deletes session entry and all associated trace files.
Export exits 1 with SESSION_NOT_FOUND if the named session does not exist.

functionalRequirements.description: Unconditional hard-block of all operations involving ZohoCorp-domain accounts.
details: Detection rule: email.Split('@')[1].Split('.')[0].Equals("zohocorp", OrdinalIgnoreCase). Covers all datacenter TLDs automatically.
Blocked at account add: check applied after email fetched from Zoho user-info API; block fires before any keychain write.
Blocked at api call (active account and --account override): check applied before any HTTP request.
Blocked at any scope subcommand: account resolved first; block fires before any mutation.
Error: ACCOUNT_DOMAIN_BLOCKED, exit 1, stderr JSON envelope.
Detection rule is a compile-time constant; cannot be disabled by flag, env var, or config.
Startup warning emitted to stderr if accounts.json contains a ZohoCorp-domain account legacy entry.

For the OAuth path: AaaServer.profile.READ is mandatory in the PKCE scope request to guarantee the email is returned from GET /oauth/user/info; the received OAuth access token is used to call this endpoint.
Fail closed: if user-info returns no email (absent or empty) for any auth type, account add fails with EMAIL_REQUIRED (exit 1) before any keychain write — the ZohoCorp check is never skipped.

functionalRequirements.description: Compile-time sealed allowlist of Zoho host suffixes; pre-request check prevents SSRF and credential exfiltration.
details: Allowed suffixes: .zoho.com, .zoho.eu, .zoho.in, .zoho.com.au, .zohoapis.com, .zohoapis.in.
Check applied in ApiClient before every outgoing HTTP request — before any TCP connection or token read.
Hosts not matching any suffix produce HOST_NOT_ALLOWED, exit 1; no network I/O performed.
The allowlist is a static readonly sealed array in ZapiCli.Core — not extensible at runtime.
Suffix matching covers all current and future subdomains under each root automatically.

functionalRequirements.description: All commands write only valid JSON to stdout (success) and stderr (error). No plain text in any code path.
details: Success envelope: {"status":"ok","data":<payload>}
Error envelope: {"error":"<message>","code":"<SYMBOLIC_CODE>","exitCode":<n>}
Symbolic error codes: ACCOUNT_NOT_FOUND, AUTH_FAILURE, NEEDS_REAUTH, HOST_NOT_ALLOWED, ACCOUNT_DOMAIN_BLOCKED, INVALID_ARGS, SESSION_NOT_FOUND, SCOPE_NOT_FOUND.
Exit codes: 0 = success, 1 = general error / security block, 2 = auth failure / needs-reauth.
No ANSI escape codes, progress spinners, or human-formatted text on stdout in any code path.

functionalRequirements.description: Global --no-input flag prevents interactive prompts; required for agent-mode invocations.
details: --no-input is a global flag accepted by all commands.
When set, any code path that would prompt for interactive input instead exits 1 with a structured JSON error.
Safe to always pass in agent invocations — has no effect on commands that never prompt.
Recommended default for all agent skill manifests.

functionalRequirements.description: Lightweight utility subcommands for agent use.
details: util time-ms: outputs {"ts": <unix_ms>} — current UTC time as Unix millisecond timestamp.
util uuid: outputs {"uuid": "<uuid-v4-string>"} — random RFC 4122 UUID v4.

functionalRequirements.description: OAuthProvider as a drop-in IAuthProvider replacement; API-based terminal flow; no browser required.
details: OAuthProvider implements IAuthProvider; ApiClient and all command classes require no changes.
client_id and client_secret are compile-time constants in OAuthProvider.cs — never user-supplied.
account add --auth-type oauth triggers PKCE flow automatically; --token flag not accepted.
account re-auth --name <n>: exchanges new token via Zoho OAuth API; sets needs_reauth=false.
OAuth tokens stored in OS keychain: zapi-cli:<accountName>:oauth.
No browser window, redirect URL, or local HTTP server required at any point.

After PKCE flow completion, an OAuth access token is received; this token is immediately used to call GET https://accounts.{domain}/oauth/user/info to fetch the account email for ZohoCorp domain validation (same email-sourcing strategy as the PAT path).

functionalRequirements.description: Named Pex/WMS WebSocket connections with per-account JSONL event buffering and drain.
details: pex connect [--account <n>]: opens Pex/WMS WebSocket; buffers events to <configDir>/zapi-cli/pex-buffer/<account>.jsonl.
pex drain [--account <n>]: atomically reads and truncates buffer; returns events as JSON array; appends pex trace entries to active session.
pex clear [--account <n>]: discards buffer without returning events.
pex listen [--account <n>]: streams events to stdout as JSONL (blocking; Ctrl+C to stop).
pex send --message <m> [--account <n>]: sends raw message over the Pex socket.
pex close [--account <n>]: closes WebSocket.
Token values never appear in Pex buffer files.

functionalRequirements.description: Local catalogue of named Zoho API endpoints with base URL, method, URL template, and purpose.
details:
api registry add --id --base-url --method --url-template --purpose

: upserts entry into registry.json.
api registry list: returns all entries as JSON array.
api registry show --id <id>: returns single entry.
api registry remove --id <id>: deletes entry; REGISTRY_ENTRY_NOT_FOUND if not exists.
Each registry entry carries a baseUrl field enabling multi-product entries in a single registry.
Enables --id desk-list-tickets shorthand form on api call in v2+

functionalRequirements.description: Named generic WebSocket connections with connect, send, listen, and close subcommands.
details: ws connect --url <url> --name <n> [--account <n>]: opens named WebSocket connection.
ws send --name <n> --message <m>: sends message over named connection.
ws listen --name <n>: streams incoming messages to stdout as JSONL (blocking).
ws close --name <n>: closes named connection.

stdout.notes: No plain text, no ANSI escape sequences, no styled terminal output in any success code path.

stderr.notes: Authorization header values unconditionally excluded from all output and trace files.

exitCodes.meaning: General error or security block (ACCOUNT_DOMAIN_BLOCKED, HOST_NOT_ALLOWED, INVALID_ARGS, etc.)

commandTree.description: zapi-cli v1 command surface. Global flags: --account, --json, --no-input, --help, --version.
v2additions: zapi-cli account add --auth-type oauth  (OAuth2 PKCE, no --token)

files.description: Account metadata — name, domain, email, is_default, needs_reauth, scopes[], token_type. Token values never stored here.
Session registry — name, status (active/closed), start_time, entry_count.
Append-only JSONL trace entries for each session. Authorization headers always excluded.
AES-256-GCM encrypted PAT/OAuth token file — fallback when OS keychain is unavailable.
API registry catalogue — named endpoints with baseUrl, method, URL template, purpose (v2).
Pex/WMS event buffer per account (v2). Atomically read and truncated by pex drain.

technologyDecisions.keyConsequence: Cross-platform single binary via dotnet publish -r <rid> /p:PublishSingleFile=true --self-contained true; nullable reference types enforced; P/Invoke to OS keychain APIs is first-class without native addon build toolchain

technologyDecisions.decision: Pluggable IAuthProvider with PatAuthProvider in v1; OAuthProvider as v2 drop-in
technologyDecisions.keyConsequence: IAuthProvider decouples auth mechanics from ApiClient and command layer; adding OAuth in v2 requires no changes to ApiClient or any command; OAuth client_id / client_secret are compile-time constants, never user-supplied

technologyDecisions.decision: --base-url required on every api call; no product-to-subdomain derivation
technologyDecisions.keyConsequence: Zero inference — caller has complete control over target URL; no stale product/datacenter mapping to maintain; ApiTraceEntry records base_url faithfully for multi-product session filtering

technologyDecisions.decision: OS-native keychain via P/Invoke, no third-party NuGet keychain package
technologyDecisions.keyConsequence: Security.framework (macOS), CredWrite/CredRead advapi32.dll (Windows), libsecret (Linux); AES-256-GCM encrypted file fallback for headless/CI; fully self-contained binary

technologyDecisions.decision: Hard-block ZohoCorp accounts — compile-time constant, no runtime override
technologyDecisions.keyConsequence: SLD label detection covers all current and future datacenter TLDs; check enforced at account add (before keychain write) and api call (before HTTP request); not bypassable via flag, env var, or config

technologyDecisions.decision: Compile-time sealed HTTP host allowlist for SSRF prevention
technologyDecisions.keyConsequence: Allowed suffixes: .zoho.com, .zoho.eu, .zoho.in, .zoho.com.au, .zohoapis.com, .zohoapis.in; HOST_NOT_ALLOWED pre-request if no match; eliminates SSRF risk and prevents credential exfiltration to non-Zoho hosts
No per-call --trace flag needed; silent drop when no session active; named developer-readable sessions; non-destructive export; Authorization header always excluded from JSONL entries

solutionProjects.name: ZapiCli
solutionProjects.role: Entry point; DI composition root; Spectre.Console.Cli command tree registration; Program.cs

solutionProjects.name: ZapiCli.Core
solutionProjects.role: Domain logic: IAuthProvider, PatAuthProvider, AccountStore, AccountConfig, ApiClient, ApiRegistry, TraceSession, TraceWriter, TraceEntry, TraceExporter, ZohoCorp domain-block utility, output contracts, error codes. Unit-testable with no OS or real HTTP dependencies.

solutionProjects.name: ZapiCli.Keychain
solutionProjects.role: IKeychainProvider + platform implementations: MacOsKeychainProvider (Security.framework), WindowsKeychainProvider (advapi32.dll), LinuxKeychainProvider (libsecret), EncryptedFileKeychainProvider (AES-256-GCM fallback)

keyAbstractions.contract: GetTokenAsync(accountName) → bearer token injected as Authorization: Zoho-oauthtoken <token>

keyAbstractions.role: HTTP dispatch layer; enforces host allowlist (pre-request, pre-token-read), ZohoCorp block, needs_reauth block, and Authorization injection; wraps response in JSON envelope; calls TraceWriter if session active
Appends ApiTraceEntry to active session JSONL file; unconditionally strips Authorization header; silently skips when no session is active
Reads and writes accounts.json; per-account CRUD; needs_reauth lifecycle management; is_default single-selection invariant

milestones.teamComposition: 1 engineer: full-stack C# / .NET 10, CLI framework, keychain P/Invoke, security logic, tests

phases.name: Core domain layer
tasks: Scaffold solution: ZapiCli, ZapiCli.Core, ZapiCli.Keychain projects with dotnet new and project references.
Implement IKeychainProvider + all four platform implementations (MacOsKeychainProvider, WindowsKeychainProvider, LinuxKeychainProvider, EncryptedFileKeychainProvider).
Implement AccountStore (read/write accounts.json, per-account CRUD, needs_reauth lifecycle).
Implement ZohoCorp domain-block utility (compile-time constant, no runtime override).

phases.name: API client + security + trace
tasks: Implement ApiClient: host allowlist check (pre-request, pre-token-read), auth header injection, HttpClient wrapper, response serialization.
Wire TraceWriter into ApiClient: append ApiTraceEntry to active session JSONL when a session is open; silently drop when none is active.
Implement TraceSession (sessions.json index read/write), TraceWriter (append-only JSONL), TraceExporter (non-destructive JSON array export).

phases.name: Command layer
tasks: Wire Spectre.Console.Cli in Program.cs; DI composition root.
Implement all account subcommands: add, list, remove, show, set-default.
Implement all scope subcommands: add, remove, list.
Implement all trace session subcommands: start, list, export, close, remove.
Implement util time-ms and util uuid.
Enforce --no-input global flag; enforce JSON-only stdout and JSON-envelope stderr across all commands.

phases.name: Tests + smoke
tasks: Unit tests: AccountStoreTests, PatAuthProviderTests, ApiClientTests (allowlist, domain-block, token-masking, trace-append paths).
Smoke test: full agent workflow on local machine (account add → api call against a live Zoho API → trace export).
Verify self-contained publish: dotnet publish -r osx-arm64 /p:PublishSingleFile=true --self-contained true.

userCentric: An agent can complete a multi-step Zoho API workflow (account resolve → api call → trace export) without any interactive prompt or error.
trace session export produces a valid, parseable JSON array after a multi-call session.
account add with a ZohoCorp email is rejected 100% of the time before any keychain write.
business: Binary builds and runs successfully on all four RIDs: win-x64, osx-x64, osx-arm64, linux-x64.
All v1 commands are implemented and reachable via the CLI by end of day 1.
technical: All stdout is valid, parseable JSON for every command path (success and error).
No PAT or OAuth token value appears in accounts.json, stdout, stderr, or any trace .jsonl file.
Host allowlist check fires pre-request, before any TCP connection is opened or any token is read from the keychain.
Unit tests pass for AccountStore, PatAuthProvider, and ApiClient (including allowlist and domain-block paths).

userStories.title: Add a PAT account
userStories.description: As an AI agent or developer, I want to add a named Zoho account using a Personal Access Token so that subsequent API calls are authenticated without any interactive login flow.
acceptanceCriteria: zapi-cli account add --name work --auth-type pat --token <PAT> succeeds and outputs {"status":"ok","data":{"name":"work"}} to stdout.
The PAT is stored in the OS keychain (or encrypted file fallback) under the key zapi-cli:work:pat.
The PAT value is never written to accounts.json.
The Zoho user-info API is called to fetch the account email; if the email matches the ZohoCorp SLD, the command fails with ACCOUNT_DOMAIN_BLOCKED (exit 1) before any keychain write.
Supplying --token together with --auth-type oauth returns a validation error (exit 1).
--domain defaults to zoho.com if not provided.

userStories.title: List accounts
userStories.description: As a developer, I want to list all configured accounts so that I can confirm what accounts are available and which is set as default.
acceptanceCriteria: zapi-cli account list outputs a JSON array of account entries to stdout.
Token values are masked as '***' in the output.
The is_default field correctly reflects the active account.
Exits 0 on success; exits 1 if accounts.json is unreadable.

userStories.title: Remove an account
userStories.description: As a developer, I want to remove a named account and its stored credentials so that no trace of that account remains on the machine.
acceptanceCriteria: zapi-cli account remove --name work deletes the account entry from accounts.json and calls DeleteAsync on the keychain provider for the account's token key.
Output confirms removal as JSON to stdout.
If the account is not found, exits 1 with a JSON error indicating the account does not exist.

userStories.title: Show account details
userStories.description: As a developer, I want to inspect a single account's metadata so that I can verify its configuration without exposing the token.
acceptanceCriteria: zapi-cli account show --name work outputs the full AccountEntry JSON with "token": "***".
No token value appears anywhere in the output.
Exits 1 with a JSON error if the account is not found.

userStories.title: Set the default account
userStories.description: As a developer, I want to designate one account as the default so that I don't have to pass --account on every command.
acceptanceCriteria: zapi-cli account set-default --name work sets is_default: true on the named account and is_default: false on all others in accounts.json.
Output confirms the change as JSON.
Exits 1 if the named account does not exist.

userStories.title: Per-command account override
userStories.description: As an AI agent, I want to override the active account for a single command so that I can operate on multiple accounts in one workflow without changing the default.
acceptanceCriteria: Any command that resolves an account accepts --account <name> to override the default for that invocation only.
accounts.json is not mutated by the override.
If the named account does not exist, the command exits 1 with a JSON error.

userStories.title: Add a scope to an account
userStories.description: As an AI agent or developer, I want to record OAuth scope strings on an account so that the scope list is available for future OAuth re-auth flows.
acceptanceCriteria: zapi-cli scope add --scope ZohoDesk.Tickets.READ [--account work] appends the scope to the account's scopes array in accounts.json and sets needs_reauth: true.
Duplicate scope entries are not added.
Output confirms the updated scope list as JSON.

userStories.title: Remove a scope from an account
userStories.description: As an AI agent or developer, I want to remove a scope from an account so that the scope list stays accurate.
acceptanceCriteria: zapi-cli scope remove --scope ZohoDesk.Tickets.READ [--account work] removes the scope and sets needs_reauth: true.
If the scope is not present, exits 1 with a JSON error.

userStories.title: List scopes for an account
userStories.description: As an AI agent, I want to list the scopes associated with an account so that I know what permissions are configured.
acceptanceCriteria: zapi-cli scope list [--account work] outputs the account's scopes array as JSON.
Exits 0 even if the scopes array is empty.

userStories.title: Block API call when re-auth is required
userStories.description: As the system, I want to block api call when the target account has pending scope changes so that the agent is notified to re-authenticate before making calls.
acceptanceCriteria: api call targeting an account with needs_reauth: true exits 2 with NEEDS_REAUTH and a message directing the user to run account re-auth --name <account>.
No HTTP request is made; no token is read from the keychain.

userStories.title: Make a GET API call
userStories.description: As an AI agent, I want to make an authenticated GET request to a Zoho product API so that I can retrieve data for analysis.
acceptanceCriteria: zapi-cli api call --base-url https://cliq.zoho.com/api/v2 --method GET --path /channels constructs the URL as https://cliq.zoho.com/api/v2/channels, injects Authorization: Zoho-oauthtoken <PAT>, and returns the HTTP response as JSON to stdout.
Exits 0 on HTTP 2xx; exits 1 on HTTP 4xx/5xx with the error response included in the stderr JSON envelope.
If an active trace session exists, an ApiTraceEntry is appended to the session .jsonl (without the Authorization value).

userStories.title: Make a POST API call with a JSON body
userStories.description: As an AI agent, I want to POST a JSON payload to a Zoho product API to create or update resources.
acceptanceCriteria: zapi-cli api call --base-url https://crm.zoho.com/crm/v5 --method POST --path /Leads --body '{"data":[{"Last_Name":"Doe"}]}' sends the body with Content-Type: application/json and returns the response JSON.
--body and --body-file supplied together exits 1 with a validation error before any network activity.
--body-file <path> reads the file and sends its contents as the request body.

userStories.title: Supply custom headers and query parameters
userStories.description: As an AI agent, I want to add custom request headers and query parameters to an API call so that I can pass required metadata or pagination controls.
acceptanceCriteria: --header X-Custom-Header:value is repeatable and appends the header to the outgoing request.
--query page=2 is repeatable and is appended to the request URL as a query string.
Custom headers do not overwrite the Authorization header.

userStories.title: Enforce host allowlist (SSRF prevention)
userStories.description: As the system, I want to reject any api call whose target host is not in the Zoho allowlist so that the tool cannot be used to send Zoho credentials to arbitrary hosts.
acceptanceCriteria: Any --base-url whose host does not end with .zoho.com, .zoho.eu, .zoho.in, .zoho.com.au, .zohoapis.com, or .zohoapis.in is rejected with HOST_NOT_ALLOWED (exit 1) before any TCP connection is opened or any token is read from the keychain.
The allowlist is hardcoded and cannot be extended without a source code change.
The check fires even if --no-input is not set.

userStories.title: Block ZohoCorp account operations
userStories.description: As the system, I want to prevent any account whose email resolves to the ZohoCorp corporate domain from being used so that Zoho corporate infrastructure is never exposed to agent-driven API calls.
acceptanceCriteria: account add fetching a ZohoCorp email from the Zoho user-info API exits 1 with ACCOUNT_DOMAIN_BLOCKED before writing to accounts.json or the keychain.
api call with an active or named ZohoCorp account exits 1 with ACCOUNT_DOMAIN_BLOCKED before any HTTP request.
scope add/remove/list targeting a ZohoCorp account exits 1 with ACCOUNT_DOMAIN_BLOCKED.
There is no flag, environment variable, or config value that bypasses the check.
A startup warning is emitted to stderr if accounts.json contains a ZohoCorp-domain account.

userStories.title: Start a named trace session
userStories.description: As an AI agent, I want to start a named trace session before a workflow run so that all API calls in that run are automatically captured.
acceptanceCriteria: zapi-cli trace session start --name desk-exploration-001 creates the session entry in sessions.json and the traces/desk-exploration-001/ directory with an empty trace.jsonl.
Subsequent api call commands automatically append entries to this session's .jsonl without any extra flag.
Starting a session when one is already active replaces the active session pointer (the old session is not destroyed).
Output confirms session creation as JSON.

userStories.title: Export a trace session
userStories.description: As an AI agent or developer, I want to export a trace session as a JSON array so that I can inspect or pass the full call log to analysis tools.
acceptanceCriteria: zapi-cli trace session export --name desk-exploration-001 emits a JSON array of ApiTraceEntry objects to stdout.
The export is non-destructive; the .jsonl file is not modified.
No Authorization header value appears in any entry's request_headers.
--truncate-body <bytes> trims response_body and request_body to the specified byte count.
--type api filters entries to API calls only.
Exits 1 with SESSION_NOT_FOUND if the named session does not exist.

userStories.title: List trace sessions
userStories.description: As a developer, I want to list all trace sessions with their metadata so that I can identify which sessions contain relevant call data.
acceptanceCriteria: zapi-cli trace session list outputs a JSON array with each session's name, start time, entry count, and status (active or closed).
Exits 0 even if no sessions exist (returns an empty array).

userStories.title: Close a trace session
userStories.description: As an AI agent, I want to close a trace session after a workflow run so that future API calls do not add entries to it.
acceptanceCriteria: zapi-cli trace session close --name desk-exploration-001 marks the session status as closed in sessions.json.
The .jsonl file is preserved for future export.
api call commands after closing no longer append entries to the closed session (they are silently dropped if no new session is started).

userStories.title: Remove a trace session
userStories.description: As a developer, I want to delete a trace session and all its associated data to free up disk space.
acceptanceCriteria: zapi-cli trace session remove --name desk-exploration-001 deletes the session entry from sessions.json and removes the traces/desk-exploration-001/ directory and its contents.
Exits 1 with SESSION_NOT_FOUND if the named session does not exist.

userStories.title: Non-interactive mode
userStories.description: As an AI agent, I want to guarantee the CLI never prompts for interactive input so that automated invocations never block waiting for user input.
acceptanceCriteria: --no-input is a global flag accepted by all commands.
When --no-input is set, any code path that would prompt for user input instead exits 1 with a structured JSON error.
The flag has no effect on commands that never prompt (safe to always pass).

userStories.title: Structured JSON output contract
userStories.description: As an AI agent, I want every CLI invocation to produce machine-parseable JSON so that I can reliably process results without text parsing.
acceptanceCriteria: All successful output is written to stdout as valid JSON (object or array).
All errors are written to stderr as { "error": "<message>", "code": "<CODE>", "exitCode": <n> }.
Exit code 0 = success; exit code 1 = general error or security block; exit code 2 = auth failure or needs-reauth.
No ANSI escape codes, progress spinners, or human-formatted text appears on stdout.

userStories.title: Get current UTC time as millisecond timestamp
userStories.description: As an AI agent, I want to retrieve the current UTC time as a Unix millisecond timestamp so that I can generate consistent timestamps for API payloads without depending on platform shell utilities.
acceptanceCriteria: zapi-cli util time-ms outputs {"ts": <unix_ms>} to stdout.
The value is a valid Unix timestamp in milliseconds for the current UTC time.
Exits 0.

userStories.title: Generate a UUID v4
userStories.description: As an AI agent, I want to generate a random UUID v4 so that I can create unique identifiers for API payloads or session names.
acceptanceCriteria: zapi-cli util uuid outputs {"uuid": "<uuid-v4-string>"} to stdout.
The value is a valid RFC 4122 UUID v4.
Exits 0.
